data.title: China Reports Major Increase In Gold, Nickel And Rhenium Reserves
data.description:
China has reported a sharp increase in its reserves of gold, nickel and other strategic minerals following a nationwide reassessment of mineral deposits, state news agency Xinhua reported on Saturday.

The assessment found that retained rhenium resources had increased by more than 200%, while additions to gold and nickel reserves were equivalent to 50 and 30 large deposits, respectively, based on data released by the Ministry of Natural Resources.

Resources of gallium, indium, tantalum and vanadium also increased, each by an amount equivalent to more than 10 large deposits, following a reassessment of associated, lower-grade and previously difficult-to-exploit resources.

According to Bloomberg, the year-long project covered 17 strategic minerals across more than 1,800 operating mines and large and medium-sized mining areas. It involved more than 100 institutions and nearly 2,000 survey personnel across 27 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities.

Separately, China discovered its first paleofluvial-lacustrine zircon placer deposit in Baicheng, Xinjiang, which could significantly increase domestic zircon supply.

China has traditionally relied heavily on imported zircon, a source of zirconium used in nuclear reactor fuel-rod cladding and high-temperature aerospace alloys.

Rhenium is also a strategic metal used in high-temperature superalloys for jet-engine components.

The reassessment included deposits previously considered low-grade or difficult to exploit, meaning the reported increases reflect expanded resource estimates rather than necessarily new discoveries.

data.title: Gold Futures Risk Falling To US$3,800, Outlook Remains Weak
data.description:
COMEX gold futures could extend their decline towards US$3,800 per ounce as selling pressure intensifies, with RHB Research maintaining its bearish outlook on the precious metal amid weakening technical indicators.

In its latest technical analysis, the research house said gold fell US$20.20 to close at US$4,031.40 per ounce on Thursday (Oct 29), moving closer to the critical US$4,000 support level.

Gold opened the session at US$4,081.40 and briefly touched an intraday high of US$4,081.70 before retreating to a low of US$4,016.30.

The metal subsequently closed at US$4,031.40, forming a long bearish candlestick that indicated continued selling pressure.

RHB said the latest price movement suggested that market sentiment remained weak, raising the possibility of a renewed downward trend.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) was also turning lower, signalling that negative momentum was beginning to accelerate again.

RHB identified US$4,000 as the immediate support level for COMEX gold, warning that a breach could trigger a deeper correction towards US$3,800.

The research house noted that the downward-trending 20-day simple moving average (SMA) would likely limit any technical rebound, reinforcing the prevailing negative outlook.

On the upside, immediate resistance is located at US$4,200, followed by a stronger resistance level at US$4,300.

RHB expects selling pressure to persist unless gold stages a sustained recovery above these resistance levels.

Given the weakening technical outlook, RHB recommended that traders retain the short position initiated at US$4,284.80 on Sept 23, with a stop-loss threshold of US$4,300 to manage trading risks.

At the latest closing price of US$4,031.40, gold has declined US$253.40, or approximately 5.9%, from the recommended short-entry level.

The research house maintained that the precious metal remained vulnerable to further losses as bearish momentum strengthened.

RHB said a decisive break below US$4,000 could open the way for a decline towards US$3,800, while any near-term recovery would likely encounter resistance from the downward-trending moving average.

data.title: South Korea’s Kospi Plunges 206.92 Points As AI Sell-Off Hammers Chip Giants
data.description:
South Korean stocks tumbled more than 3% on Oct 30, as a global semiconductor sell-off and mounting concerns over the sustainability of artificial intelligence (AI) investments triggered heavy foreign selling.

According to Yonhap, the benchmark Kospi plunged 206.92 points, or 3.48%, to close at 5,730.74, after sinking to an intraday low of 5,599.42. The sharp decline prompted the Korea Exchange to activate a sell-side trading curb shortly after 10am as futures prices slumped.

The rout followed overnight losses on Wall Street, where Google parent Alphabet plunged more than 12% after disappointing quarterly revenue raised fresh concerns over returns on massive AI investments. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.38%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index shed 1.4%.

South Korean chipmakers bore the brunt of the selling, with Samsung Electronics sliding 3.02% to 225,000 won and SK hynix sinking 7.08% to 1.42 million won.

Automotive stocks also came under pressure. Hyundai Motor declined 3.59% to 282,000 won after cutting its annual sales target and investment plans, while Kia plunged 11.73% to 95,600 won following weaker-than-expected third-quarter operating profit.

Defence giant Hanwha Aerospace slumped 8.42% to 696,000 won after disappointing quarterly earnings linked to delayed deliveries of K9 self-propelled howitzers to Poland.

Foreign investors offloaded a net 1.62 trillion won worth of shares, outweighing net purchases of 742.55 billion won by institutions and 620.97 billion won by retail investors.

Market breadth was sharply negative, with 655 decliners against 232 gainers. Trading volume reached 212.76 million shares worth 19.27 trillion won (US$14.44 billion).

data.title: Hong Kong Stocks Rebound 335.77 Points as Consumer, Energy Shares Lift Hang Seng
data.description:
Hong Kong stocks rebounded strongly on Oct 30, with the benchmark Hang Seng Index climbing 335.77 points, or 1.46%, to close at 23,294.42, driven by gains in consumer, energy and shipping stocks as investors snapped up beaten-down shares following recent market weakness.

The rally was supported by bargain hunting in technology heavyweights, including Alibaba and Tencent, alongside renewed buying interest in consumer-related stocks and stronger corporate earnings.

Consumer stocks led the advance, with China Mengniu Dairy surging 9.4%, while Nongfu Spring and Tingyi gained more than 5%. Energy counters also strengthened, with Sinopec advancing over 6% and PetroChina rising more than 5%, supported by encouraging earnings and improved sentiment towards the sector.

Shipping and port operators contributed to the gains, with COSCO Shipping Holdings climbing 7.7% and COSCO Shipping Ports advancing 7.4%, amid expectations of stronger freight rates.

However, technology stocks posted mixed performances as concerns over heavy artificial intelligence investment spending and valuations continued to weigh on semiconductor-related counters. Lenovo Group tumbled more than 7%, while SMIC declined 4.4%.

The Hang Seng Tech Index edged up 0.29% to 3,754.90 points, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index advanced 1.37% to 7,862.22 points.

Market turnover reached HK$214.3 billion, although southbound investors recorded net selling of approximately HK$3.56 billion.

Despite the rebound, the Hang Seng Index ended October down 5.36%, while the Hang Seng Tech Index suffered a steeper monthly decline of 11.73%, reflecting persistent concerns over global technology valuations, elevated US Treasury yields and uncertainty surrounding China’s economic recovery.

data.title: Singapore Stocks Slip 0.4% as Tech Sell-Off, Banking Losses Weigh on STI
data.description:
Singapore shares closed lower on Oct 30, as a regional technology sell-off and weakness in banking stocks weighed on investor sentiment amid growing concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) spending and corporate earnings.

The benchmark Straits Times Index (STI) declined 0.4% to 5,376.74 points, dragged down by losses across major financial counters and semiconductor-related stocks.

The decline followed a sharp sell-off on Wall Street, where investors retreated from AI-linked stocks amid concerns over heavy capital expenditure and uncertain investment returns. Alphabet’s 12.6% plunge in the previous US session further dampened sentiment across Asian technology markets.

Singapore’s semiconductor-related counters came under significant pressure, with AEM falling 8.6% to S$7.45, UMS Integration shedding 7.8% to S$2.01 and Frencken declining 5.2% to S$2.01.

Banking heavyweights also contributed to the benchmark’s losses. DBS slipped 0.9% to S$73.13, OCBC eased 0.2% to S$29.29, while UOB declined 0.3% to S$41.37.

Wilmar International was the STI’s biggest decliner, losing 3.2% to S$3.01, while Mapletree Logistics Trust bucked the trend, advancing 2.8% to S$1.10.

Market breadth remained negative, with 304 decliners outnumbering 270 gainers. Total trading volume reached 1.1 billion securities worth S$1.9 billion.

data.title: Wall Street Closes Sharply Lower Amid AI Cash Burn
data.description:
US stocks ​tumbled on Oct 30, with the Nasdaq suffering its largest one-day percentage drop since June 5 following disappointing quarterly results from ‌Intel and Amazon, which amplified growing worries surrounding artificial intelligence (AI)-related companies’ massive spending on the nascent technology.

All three major US stock indexes slumped, with the Nasdaq sliding 2.9%. The tech-heavy index has dropped 7.8% from its all-time closing high reached on October 6.

The tech rout was sparked by disappointing quarterly results from Intel and Amazon released late on ​Oct 29. While Amazon pared losses as the session progressed, Intel shares plunged 28.6%.

Chip stocks veered sharply lower, with Nvidia down 4.2% ​and AMD sliding 10.9%. The broader chips index shed 7.2%, slumping to a monthly loss of more than ⁠15%. Server makers Dell and HP dropped 10.8% and 9.6%, respectively.

All three main equity indexes closed lower on the week. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq logged monthly losses, while the Dow exited October with a gain.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 572.25 points, or 1.09%, to 51,770.31, the S&P 500 lost 140.32 points, or 1.82%, to 7,580.07 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 747.73 points, or 2.86%, to 25,437.00.

The S&P 500 tech sector posted its largest monthly percentage loss since March 2025, and communication services registered its biggest monthly drop since April 2022.

Third-quarter earnings season has passed the halfway mark, with 299 companies in the S&P 500 having reported. Of those, 82% have beaten consensus expectations, according to LSEG data.

Analysts now expect third-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth of 31.6%, year-on-year, per LSEG.

Oil supermajors Exxon Mobil and Chevron both beat quarterly profit expectations, benefiting from soaring profit margins as a result of energy supply disruptions arising from the US-Israeli war with Iran and Russia’s war in Ukraine. The stocks gained 2.2% and 2.8%, respectively.

Starbucks dipped 1.8% after the coffee chain forecast an annual revenue decline due to its divestiture of its Chinese business.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.8-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange. There were 169 new highs and 377 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 1,196 stocks rose and 3,622 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.03-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 43 new 52-week highs and 5 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 70 new highs and 355 new lows.

Volume on US exchanges was 19.87 billion shares, compared with the 17.26 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

Reuters

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Closes Higher As Banking Stocks Lift FBM KLCI
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia ended Oct 30 on a positive note, with the benchmark index climbing 4.44 points as renewed buying interest in banking and selected blue-chip stocks lifted market sentiment despite mixed regional performance.

At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 4.44 points, or 0.28%, to 1,615.60 from the previous day’s close of 1,611.16.

The benchmark index traded between 1,606.72 and 1,620.76 during the session, recovering from earlier weakness to finish in positive territory.

The broader indices, however, ended mixed, with the FBM 70 declining 63.18 points, or 0.36%, to 17,420.94, reflecting continued selling pressure among mid-cap stocks, while the F4GBM gained 0.84 point, or 0.09%, to 977.57 and the FBM Emas edged up 5.88 points, or 0.05%, to 12,061.77.

The FBM Shariah slipped 1.31 points, or 0.01%, to 12,082.97, highlighting mixed performance across the broader market.

Zetrix AI Bhd emerged as the most actively traded counter, with 421.12 million shares changing hands. The stock fell 1.5 sen to 6.5 sen. GIIB Holdings Bhd followed with 95.94 million shares traded, plunging 18 sen to 36 sen, while JAKS Resources Bhd slipped half a sen to 14.5 sen on 94.43 million shares.

Ni Hsin Group Bhd declined 11 sen to 26 sen, with 66.37 million shares exchanged, while MAG Holdings Bhd remained unchanged at 15.5 sen on 55.39 million shares.

All five most actively traded counters finished either lower or unchanged, underscoring persistent selling pressure among lower-priced stocks despite the benchmark index’s gains.

Trading activity strengthened, with total turnover increasing to 3.15 billion shares worth RM2.68 billion compared to 2.95 billion shares valued at RM2.43 billion on Oct 29.

The stronger close reflected selective buying in banking and blue-chip counters, although weakness in mid-cap and actively traded stocks continued to weigh on broader market sentiment.

data.title: Losers Outnumber Gainers Amid Broad Market Weakness
data.description:
The market closed the trading session on Oct 30 on a mixed note, with Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI) leading the decliners while Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) topped the gainers’ list amid persistent selling pressure across the broader market.

Market breadth remained negative, with 648 losers against 430 gainers, while 501 counters were unchanged, 1,201 untraded and 66 suspended.

MPI was the biggest casualty, plunging RM1.72 to RM39.78, followed by Mega Fortris Bhd, which tumbled 52 sen to RM2.22.

UWC Bhd declined 49 sen to RM7.15, while British American Tobacco (Malaysia) Bhd shed 40 sen to RM3.74. Mi Technovation Bhd rounded out the five biggest losers, slipping 33 sen to RM6.53.

On the positive side, plantation heavyweight KLK led the gainers, rising 44 sen to RM20.96, followed by Ayer Holdings Bhd, which advanced 35 sen to RM8.10.

APM Automotive Holdings Bhd climbed 25 sen to RM2.60, while United Plantations Bhd gained 22 sen to RM29.22. Petronas Dagangan Bhd completed the top five gainers, adding 16 sen to RM19.50.

Trading activity strengthened despite the negative market breadth, with total turnover increasing to 3.15 billion shares worth RM2.68 billion compared to Oct 29’s 2.95 billion shares valued at RM2.43 billion.

The contrasting performances highlighted selective buying in plantation and other heavyweight counters, even as selling pressure continued to weigh on technology and selected consumer stocks.

data.title: Gold Faces Fresh Pressure With US$4,000 Support In Focus
data.description:
Gold prices fell on Friday as higher oil prices and stronger US inflation data reinforced expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December, putting bullion on track for a second consecutive monthly decline.

Spot gold slipped 0.9% to US$3,982.85 an ounce by 7.40am GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery fell 1% to US$3,992.50. The precious metal was also heading for a weekly loss.

US inflation accelerated in September as consumers paid more for gasoline and other goods, strengthening the case for tighter monetary policy. Traders were pricing in a 72% probability of a Fed rate hike in December, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

Higher interest rates tend to weigh on gold by increasing the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding asset.

Rising oil prices added to inflation concerns, with crude heading for a fourth consecutive monthly gain following an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. The incident highlighted supply risks linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran.

KCM Trade chief market analyst Tim Waterer said gold was facing pressure around the US$4,000 support level, with the market yet to establish whether buying interest would emerge to limit further declines.

He added that stronger US economic indicators had kept the Federal Reserve on track for a potential December rate increase, while elevated oil prices were adding to the pressure on bullion.

Meanwhile, RHB Research said COMEX gold faced strong selling pressure on Thursday, falling US$20.20 to close at US$4,031.40 after trading between US$4,016.30 and US$4,081.70.

The research house described the session’s long bearish candlestick and downward-turning Relative Strength Index as signs of weakening market sentiment and accelerating negative momentum. It warned that gold could break below US$4,000 and extend its correction towards US$3,800.

RHB Research maintained its negative trading bias and advised traders to retain their short position initiated at US$4,284.80 at the close on Sept 23, with a stop-loss level of US$4,300.

It identified immediate support at US$4,000, followed by US$3,800, while resistance was pegged at US$4,200 and US$4,300.

Other precious metals also weakened on Friday. Spot silver fell 3.1% to US$50.74 an ounce, platinum dropped 3.3% to US$1,439.05 and palladium declined 2.3% to US$982.50. All three were heading for weekly and monthly losses.

data.title: Stock Today: CTOS Gives Back Gains After Previous Session’s Sharp Rebound
data.description:
CTOS Digital Bhd shares fell 3.7% in afternoon trading on Friday, giving up some of the previous session’s gains as investors continued to weigh the potential earnings impact of disruptions to selected credit reporting services following a cybersecurity incident.

As at 3.55pm, the stock was down 1.5 sen to RM0.39, compared with its last traded price of RM0.405. It opened at RM0.40 and moved between RM0.38 and RM0.405, with 13.4 million shares traded.

The decline followed a 10.26% rally on Thursday, when CTOS gained four sen to RM0.43 in morning trading.

CIMB Securities has maintained its Hold recommendation and RM0.55 target price on the counter, warning that the service disruptions and the expiry of the company’s tax incentive could weigh on fourth-quarter earnings.

The affected credit reporting activities account for approximately 35% of group revenue, with CIMB estimating that each additional week of disruption could reduce profit after tax and minority interests by RM1.3 million.

CTOS reported a 7.5% year-on-year increase in revenue to RM256 million for the nine months ended September 2026, while core net profit rose 14.6% to RM70.1 million.

Investors are also monitoring the restoration of affected services and the recovery of transaction volumes, alongside the impact of the tax incentive’s expiry on Nov 8.

data.title: FBM KLCI Rebounds At Midday Despite Weak Market Breadth
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia’s benchmark index reversed earlier losses to close the morning session marginally higher on Oct 30, buoyed by buying interest in plantation heavyweights, even as losers continued to dominate the broader market.

At 12.30pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) gained 1.15 points, or 0.07%, to 1,612.31 from its close of 1,611.16 on Oct 29, outperforming regional peers.

The benchmark index traded between 1,606.72 and 1,612.99 during the morning session.

However, broader market indices remained largely in negative territory. The FBM 70 Index slipped 20.27 points, or 0.12%, to 17,463.85, while the FBM Emas eased 2.48 points, or 0.02%, to 12,053.41.

The FBM Shariah declined 11.90 points, or 0.1%, to 12,072.38, while the F4GBM edged down 0.01 point, or approximately 0.001%, to 976.72.

Market breadth remained negative, with 602 losers against 313 gainers, while 436 counters were unchanged, 1,429 untraded and 66 suspended.

Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd emerged as the biggest loser, plunging RM1.16 to RM40.34, followed by British American Tobacco (Malaysia) Bhd, which shed 39 sen to RM3.75, and Mega Fortris Bhd, which declined 36 sen to RM2.38. Other top losers include Hong Leong Bank Bhd, which lost 28 sen to RM21.12, and UWC Bhd, which dropped 25 sen to RM7.39.

On the positive side, Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd topped the gainers’ list, climbing 38 sen to RM20.90, followed by United Plantations Bhd, which advanced 24 sen to RM29.24.

Nestlé (M) Bhd gained 22 sen to RM96.12, APM Automotive Holdings Bhd rose 21 sen to RM2.56, while Ayer Holdings Bhd added 15 sen to RM7.90.

Meanwhile, the active trading was led by Zetrix AI Bhd with approximately 200.38 million shares changing hands, falling 1.5 sen to 6.5 sen.

JAKS Resources Bhd followed with 89.39 million shares traded, easing half a sen to 14.5 sen.

GIIB Holdings Bhd saw 80.9 million shares traded, plunging 18.5 sen to 35.5 sen, while Ni Hsin Group Bhd fell 14 sen to 23 sen on 49.91 million shares.

VS Industry Bhd rounded out the five most actively traded counters, slipping one sen to 33 sen with 34.98 million shares exchanged.

Total turnover stood at 1.89 billion shares worth RM1.08 billion.

The midday performance highlighted a divergence between the benchmark index and the broader market, as selective buying in plantation heavyweights helped cushion the FBM KLCI despite persistent selling pressure across other counters.

data.title: Stock Today: SD Guthrie Edges Higher Following RM933 Million Land Disposal
data.description:
SD Guthrie Bhd rose 3 sen, or 0.52%, to RM5.80 as at 11.26am, following its proposed RM933.57 million disposal of plantation land in Bukit Kerayong, Klang, for an integrated industrial park development.

The plantation group’s shares opened at RM5.80 and traded between RM5.77 and RM5.82, with approximately 601,400 shares changing hands. The stock had closed at RM5.77 in the previous trading session.

The proposed disposal involves approximately 1,623 acres of freehold land, which will be acquired by Bukit Kerayong Industrial Developments Sdn Bhd, a joint venture involving SD Guthrie, YTL Power International Bhd and Bumi Assets Sdn Bhd.

SD Guthrie will retain a 30% stake in the venture, while YTL Power and Bumi Assets will each hold 35%. The group will also invest up to RM101.12 million through its subsidiary in the joint venture.

CIMB Securities has maintained its Buy recommendation on SD Guthrie with a target price of RM6.52, estimating that the transaction could generate RM586.3 million in net gains after consolidation adjustments.

The research house expects the disposal, alongside the group’s previously announced Kulai land sale, to support industrial development net profit of RM960 million in financial year 2027, compared with its existing forecast of RM600 million.

The potential increase of RM360 million could provide a 12% upside to SD Guthrie’s overall FY27 net profit forecast, although CIMB has yet to incorporate the full earnings uplift pending a review after the group’s third-quarter results.

CIMB also expects SD Guthrie to use approximately RM744.4 million, or 80% of the disposal proceeds, to repay debt, potentially reducing its pro forma gearing ratio from 0.24 times to 0.20 times.

data.title: Bitcoin Slides To Six-Week Low, Ethereum Hits Two-Month Low Amid Binance Hack Fears
data.description:
Bitcoin and Ethereum tumbled on Oct 30, hitting multi-week lows as fears over a suspected multibillion-dollar security breach at Binance triggered a broader cryptocurrency sell-off.

Bitcoin, the world’s largest cryptocurrency, fell around 2% in early Asian trading to a six-week low of US$77,646, while Ethereum declined by a similar margin to a two-month low of US$2,238.76.

Selling pressure intensified as investors reacted to reports that Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, had frozen approximately US$3 billion in digital assets while investigating a potential security breach.

The turmoil also weighed heavily on Binance’s native token, BNB, which plunged more than 8% over 24 hours to US$694, reflecting mounting concerns over security vulnerabilities across the digital asset industry.

Market sentiment deteriorated further as stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle moved to freeze assets linked to the suspected incident, raising questions over the scale of the potential losses.

Binance co-founder Yi He pledged that the exchange would cover hacking-related losses, while the company continued working with blockchain intelligence firms and law enforcement agencies to trace affected funds.

The sharp retreat in Bitcoin and Ethereum underscores renewed fragility in cryptocurrency markets, with investors closely monitoring developments surrounding the Binance investigation and the potential for further selling pressure.

With both cryptocurrencies trading near multi-week lows, market attention remains focused on whether prices can stabilise or face another wave of declines as uncertainty persists.

data.title: Stock Today: YTL Power Gains 0.38% Following RM933.6 Million Klang Land Deal
data.description:
YTL Power International Bhd rose 2 sen, or 0.38%, to RM5.32 as at 10.55am, following its involvement in a joint venture with SD Guthrie Bhd to develop an integrated industrial park in Bukit Kerayong, Klang.

The utility group’s shares opened at RM5.29 and traded between RM5.23 and RM5.35, with 1.75 million shares changing hands. The stock had closed at RM5.30 in the previous trading session.

The market movement followed SD Guthrie’s announcement on Thursday that it had agreed to dispose of approximately 1,623 acres of freehold plantation land in Bukit Kerayong for RM933.57 million as part of the proposed industrial development.

The project will be undertaken by Bukit Kerayong Industrial Developments Sdn Bhd, a joint venture involving YTL Power, SD Guthrie and Bumi Assets Sdn Bhd.

YTL Power’s wholly owned subsidiary, Bukit Kerayong Industrial Venture Sdn Bhd, and Bumi Assets will each hold a 35% stake in the joint venture, while SD Guthrie Land Ventures Sdn Bhd will own the remaining 30%.

The proposed development will transform the plantation land into a light-to-medium industrial park supported by commercial hubs, infrastructure and public facilities.

data.title: Yen Holds Steady Ahead Of BOJ Decision, AI Concerns Weigh On Dollar
data.description:
The yen traded steadily on Friday ahead of the Bank of Japan’s (BOJ) policy decision, while the US dollar weakened slightly as concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) spending triggered a shift towards safe-haven assets, including US Treasuries.

The Japanese currency eased marginally to around 157.815 per US dollar, with the BOJ widely expected to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 1.25%. However, investors are watching for a hawkish policy signal, with markets pricing in an approximately 80% chance of a rate increase in December.

The yen was on track to lose 0.2% against the dollar for October, while the US dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, edged down to 101.77. The index was nevertheless set for a 0.3% monthly gain, marking its second consecutive month of advances.

The dollar came under pressure from falling US Treasury yields as investors sought safety following renewed concerns over the returns from heavy AI investments. Disappointing developments from Alphabet earlier in the week weighed on technology shares and broader equity markets, increasing demand for government bonds.

The yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury note stood at 4.8958%, while the 30-year yield fell to 5.2623%. Both were at their lowest levels in more than a month.

OCBC foreign exchange strategist Sim Moh Siong said the market reaction differed from a conventional risk-off episode driven by energy concerns.

“Rather than supporting the USD and pushing US yields higher, US-centric AI concerns were accompanied by lower Treasury yields and a softer or broadly subdued USD,” he said in a note.

ANZ head of Asia research Khoon Goh said the global monetary tightening cycle was likely to continue, with elevated inflation potentially prompting further interest rate increases in 2027.

Elsewhere, the euro was little changed at US$1.1185 after touching its lowest level since May 2025 in the previous session. Sterling rose 0.1% to US$1.3390, while the Australian dollar held at US$0.7030 and the New Zealand dollar eased to US$0.5626.

Oil prices remained elevated, with Brent crude futures on track for an 11.5% gain in October, marking their fourth consecutive monthly increase and longest winning streak in more than two years.

Reuters

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Starts Steady Ahead Of Corporate Earnings
data.description:
The FBM KLCI opened marginally higher on Friday as investors remained cautious amid global market volatility, domestic political developments and expectations of a fresh round of corporate earnings, per The Star.

At 9.12am, the benchmark index gained 0.12 points to 1,611.28, with early gains led by CIMB Group Holdings, which rose seven sen to RM6.96, and IHH Healthcare, which added four sen to RM7.89.

Apex Securities said renewed pressure on the artificial intelligence trade in the United States, following disappointing developments from Alphabet and Intel, had weighed on the Nasdaq.

Geopolitical risks also remained in focus after the US flagged the possibility of taking action against Iran following the November 3 midterm elections.

Locally, investors were watching third-quarter 2026 corporate earnings and positioning their portfolios ahead of the FBM KLCI’s phased expansion from 30 to 50 constituents.

Political developments added to the cautious sentiment, with Sarawak’s state assembly dissolved ahead of its 13th state election and the Melaka state election scheduled for November 14.

Apex Securities expects the benchmark index to remain range-bound with a selective defensive bias in the near term, citing external and domestic uncertainties, including political uncertainty ahead of the 16th general election.

Among the actively traded counters, Zetrix fell one sen to seven sen, JAKS Resources slipped one sen to 14 sen, while GIIB declined 12.5 sen to 41.5 sen.

data.title: Ringgit Extends Winning Streak To 10 Days, Opens Near Seven-Week High
data.description:
The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar for the 10th consecutive trading day on Friday, extending its positive momentum and trading near a seven-week high.

At 8am, the local currency edged up to 4.0570/0625 against the greenback from Thursday’s close of 4.0575/0620. The level was close to its previous opening high of RM4.0560 recorded on Sept 9, 2026.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell 0.33% to 101.854 points despite stronger-than-expected US gross domestic product growth in the third quarter of 2026 and higher personal consumption expenditure inflation in September.

He added that US Treasury yields also declined, with the two-year yield falling 10 basis points to 4.60% and the 10-year yield easing eight basis points to 4.94%.

“Hence, we believe the market is pricing in the possibility that the Federal Reserve (Fed) might change its direction on monetary policy.

“As such, the ringgit is likely to maintain its positive trend in the near term, given the limited scope for further Fed monetary tightening. The ringgit-US dollar pair could therefore hover between RM4.05 and RM4.07 today,” he told Bernama.

Against other major currencies, the ringgit traded lower, weakening to 5.4275/4348 against the British pound from 5.4009/4069 at Thursday’s close. It also slipped to 4.5365/5427 against the euro from 4.5176/5226 and eased to 2.5707/5743 against the Japanese yen from 2.5685/5715.

Against ASEAN currencies, the ringgit was little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 223.6/224.0 and remained flat against the Philippine peso at 6.35/6.36.

However, it weakened against the Singapore dollar to 3.1700/1746 from 3.1665/1702 and slipped against the Thai baht to 12.0279/0513 from 12.0165/0345.

data.title: Singapore Shares Open Lower, STI Slips 0.01%
data.description:
Singapore shares opened slightly lower on Friday, with the benchmark Straits Times Index (STI) easing 0.01% as more stocks declined than advanced.

The STI slipped 0.68 points to 5,395.35 as at 9.12am, with 83 counters advancing against 132 decliners. Total trading volume stood at 61.67 million securities, valued at S$134.24 million.

data.title: HSIF Faces Further Downside Below 23,000, RHB
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its negative trading outlook on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), advising traders to retain their short positions as the index continues to struggle around the 23,000-point level.

HSIF fell 50 points to close at 23,024 points on Thursday after a volatile session. It opened at 23,046 points and climbed to an intraday high of 23,187 points before selling pressure pushed it down to 22,915 points. The index later recovered part of its losses, while evening trading saw it gain another 84 points to close at 23,108 points.

RHB Research said the narrow-bodied candlestick, accompanied by long upper and lower shadows, reflected indecision as buyers and sellers continued to battle around the 23,000-point mark.

The futures contract remains below its 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages (SMA), while its Relative Strength Index (RSI) continues to trend below the 50% level. The indicators suggest that bearish momentum remains dominant.

A decisive break below 23,000 points could expose HSIF to further losses towards the next support at 22,400 points, followed by 22,000 points. On the upside, any recovery is expected to encounter selling pressure at 23,600 points, with stronger resistance at 24,370 points.

RHB Research said it would maintain its negative trading bias as long as HSIF remains below 24,370 points.

Traders were advised to retain the short position initiated at the close on 17 September at 24,572 points, with the stop-loss level adjusted to 24,370 points.
